name: Fran
headline: 21-15-9 Thrusters & Pull-ups
summary: 21-15-9 thrusters and pull-ups. Short, fast and famously painful.
intro: Fran is the benchmark most people hear about first, and for good reason: two movements, 90 reps, and a finish line that arrives quickly and hurts anyway. Fast athletes are done in well under five minutes, so it rewards keeping the bar moving and holding the pull-ups in big sets. Retest it every few months and the clock tells you plainly how your engine and your gymnastics are coming along.
scaling: Lighter bar: choose a load you could thrust 21 times without stopping when fresh.
Banded or jumping pull-ups, or ring rows if pull-ups are still a work in progress.
Cut the rep scheme to 15-12-9 for newer athletes.
tips: Split the 21 thrusters before you have to (for example 11 then 10) rather than failing at rep 18.
Put the bar right next to the rig and chalk before the clock starts: transitions are where Fran times are lost.
Drive the bar up with your legs out of the squat; tired shoulders cannot press it alone.
The round of 9 is a sprint. If there is anything left, go unbroken.

name: Grace
headline: 30 Clean and Jerks for Time
summary: 30 clean and jerks at a moderate load, as fast as you can.
intro: Grace is one movement and one number: 30 clean and jerks for time. The load is heavy enough that every rep needs proper technique, yet light enough that the fastest athletes move it in around two minutes. It is a test of efficient barbell cycling and of how well you can manage your breathing between reps.
scaling: Reduce the load so that most reps can be done as quick singles with good positions.
Use dumbbells (one or two) if the barbell clean is not yet solid.
Cut the volume to 20 reps for beginners.
tips: Plan on fast singles from the start: drop, reset and go, rather than touch-and-go reps that fall apart.
Stay close to the bar and breathe at the top of each rep, not on the floor.
Pick a pace (for example one rep every 6 to 8 seconds) and hold it.

intro: Isabel takes the format of Grace and swaps in the snatch: 30 reps at a moderate load, as fast as possible. scaling: Reduce the load to one you can snatch with confidence for quick singles.
Swap in dumbbell or kettlebell snatches if the barbell snatch is still being learned.
Cut the volume to 20 reps.
tips: Fast singles are usually quicker than sets that end in a missed rep.
Keep the bar close and finish the pull before pulling yourself under.
A missed rep costs you the rep and your rhythm: stay a little under your limit.
